Factors (abbreviation)Definitions
Step 1. Unsafe ActsDecision errors (De)Behavior or actions are intended
The chosen plan is inadequate or faulty to achieve the desired results
The error is not caused by the lack of a particular skill to perform the task
Skilled-based errors (Se)Behavior or actions are unintended
The actions are related to a routine task or procedure
The errors can be reduced by training/practice
Perceptual errors (Pce)"Misperception of an object, threat or situation" including "visual/auditory/proprioceptive or vestibular illusions, cognitive or attention failures"
Routine violation (Rv)Routinely, deliberately disregard for established rules and procedures
Exceptional violation (Ev)Nonroutine violation of established rules and procedures
Step 2. Preconditions of Unsafe ActsTechnical environment (Te)The workspace or design factors that affect the actions of individuals
Physical environment (Pe)The environmental factors such as "weather/climate/white-out or dust-out" conditions that affect the actions of individuals
Hazard by others (Hbo)A hazardous condition created by parties other than the victims and unknown to the victims
Adverse mental state (Adm)Lack of mental capabilities for performing certain tasks
Adverse physiological states (Adp)Lack of physiological capabilities for performing certain tasks
Physical/mental limitations (Pml)A possible combination of "adverse mental states" and "adverse physiological states"
Crew resource management (Crm)Improper crew composition (i.e., lack of crew members with needed skills or knowledge)
Coordination/communication/leadership issues within the crew
Personal readiness (Pr)The physical fitness and stress (such as time pressure), inadequate rest
Step 3. Unsafe SupervisionInadequate supervision (Ins)Inadequate or inappropriate supervision that results in the failure of the crew member(s) to "identify a hazard, recognize and control risk"
Planned inappropriate operations (Pio)Work plan is flawed and creates unnecessary risks to jobsite crew members
The accident can be avoided by choosing a better plan without extraordinary measures
Failed to correct problem (Fcp)"Deficiencies among individuals/equipment/training or other related safety areas are 'known' to the supervisor, yet are allowed to continue uncorrected"
Supervisory violations (Sv)"Supervisors willfully disregard existing rules and regulations"
Step 4. Organizational InfluencesResource management (Rm)Issues related to the acquisition/allocation/and management of organizational resources
Organizational climate (Oc)Inadequate or improper safety organizational structure/policies/ or culture within the organization
Organizational Process (Op)Inadequate or improper formal process that deals with safety management at the management level, including "operations" (operational tempo/time pressures/incentives/disincentives etc.), "procedures (performance standards/objectives/documentation/instructions etc.)" and "oversight (monitoring and checking of resources, climate and processes)

MeasuresMeasuresClearPainting WorkWhile installing a temporary rope support on the rooftop parapet and using a suspended scaffold, the support securing the main rope became detached. During the fall, the secondary rope snapped, resulting in a fall accident.While installing a temporary rope support on the rooftop parapet and using a suspended scaffold, the worker did not properly secure the main rope, causing the support to become detached. The secondary rope also broke during the fall.

Classification typeDescription type
Step 1 Factor (abbreviation)SeThe fact that the worker did not properly secure the main rope can be viewed as a mistake in a skilled task, which corresponds to Skilled-based errors. Since this cause is explicitly mentioned, it has a high level of reliability.
Step 1 Reliability5
Step 2 Factor (abbreviation)TeThe use of a temporary rope support and a suspended scaffold pertains to the technical aspects of the work environment, classified under Technical environment. This factor is only indirectly referenced in the accident description, but it strongly suggests that the work environment likely influenced the incident.
Step 2 Reliability4
Step 3 Factor (abbreviation)InsThe improper securing of the main rope and the breaking of the secondary rope indicate insufficient supervision during the work process. This could be categorized as Inadequate supervision, but further inference is needed since there is no direct mention in the account.
Step 3 Reliability3
Step 4 Factor (abbreviation)OpThere may have been inadequate organizational processes related to safe work procedures and equipment checks. This aligns with the Organizational process category, but it requires considerable inference because there is no explicit reference in the incident details.
Step 4 Reliability2
